narrative: One year on, full-year 2019 net income set a fresh record at $36.4 billion, up from $32.5 billion in 2018. The quarter that started the case looks, so far, like a blip.

checks.a1: Supported within the year. Full-year 2019 net income reached a record $36.4 billion, extending the trend the December quarter had interrupted. A single subsequent year does not rule out a later downturn.
checks.a2: Unresolved. Full-year 2018 results already reflect the rate increases to date; the starting record cannot show whether future rate moves will keep lifting income or reverse.
checks.a3: Unresolved. A strong capital ratio and ongoing branch and technology investment at the cutoff do not by themselves show how the bank would perform through a future downturn.
checks.a4: Not supported yet. Profit rose to a record in 2019 rather than turning down, extending the cycle instead of marking its top. This does not rule out a peak arriving later.
checks.a5: Choosing not to take a position is consistent with uncertainty. This outcome alone cannot tell us whether that was the better decision.

assumptions.text: The December quarter was market noise, not the credit cycle turning.
Higher rates will keep lifting net interest income.
Scale and capital will let the bank take share through the next downturn.
Rising provisions and expenses mark the top of the earnings cycle.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.

events.headline: JPMorgan reports record full-year 2019 net income of $36.4 billion, up from $32.5 billion in 2018

source.title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. 4Q19 Earnings Release (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K)
